The model's architecture drawing, 127 vector paths: a box of numbered local nodes ('1', '2', ... 'n') with 'Inputs' arrows entering from below and 'Global Type Output' leaving upward, joined to three rectangular global nodes ('i+1', 'i+2', '...') by arrows labelled 'Global Link (i, i+1)', '(i, i+2)', '(i, ...)'; a dashed circle marks the 'Local Network' and a dashed ellipse on the right opens the 'Local View', a dense cluster of small filled nodes with its own 'Local Type Output'. The bottom left corner carries the figure's own two-entry symbol key, open rectangle = 'Global Nodes', open circle = 'Local Nodes', so the legend is inside the region [geometry.legend].

note: Seventeen measured regions over eleven pages, all accounted: 14 figure rows and 3 printed tables, no exclusions. The paper numbers its exhibits flatly - Figure 1 to Figure 10, Table 1 to Table 3 - which is the first paper in this run whose numbering fits the enum without a note. Figure 2 prints its three panels as three separate measured rasters under one caption that splits them into '(a) (b)' under 'The Increasing rates of change in human activity' and '(c)' under 'Global scale changes'; Figures 6 and 7 each print two panels as two separate regions with two identical frames. The tables are of three different constructions: Table 1 is a pasted colour raster with no rules, Table 2 a booktabs notation list, Table 3 a spanner-header grid with one vertical rule. One artwork is printed twice: the p15 Figure 9 plot is the p12 Figure 6(a) forecast reused almost pixel for pixel, so the family and the row are separate per caption but the note says the drawing repeats. No exhibit lacks a citing sentence except Figure 4, which is introduced by prose and never named. No declared gaps: the layout pass measures nothing on the pages that carry only prose.
rules: Every exhibit in this paper carries a flat number - 'Figure 1' to 'Figure 10' and 'Table 1' to 'Table 3' - so unlike the previous papers in this range the enum fits, and only Figure 1 needs the colon form 'Figure N:' because it prints 'Figure 1:' [caption.numbering].

Three of the four tables caption themselves with the bare word ('Table 1', 'Table 2', 'Table 3') and print no title line at all, so the title the reader sees is the one in the note and not in the caption [caption.verbatim].

Table 1 is a pasted colour raster whose bands are separated by fill and white gaps rather than by rules, so `rule_style` is `no-rules` and `zebra` is false even though the bands alternate in colour [table.rule_style].
Table 3 is the only table with a vertical rule (between its Input and Output halves) and the only one with a two-row spanner header, so it alone records `merged_cells` [table.merged_cells].

The two p12 panels and the two p13 panels are separate measured regions with separate frames, so each gets its own row with a panel layout rather than being folded into one `composite-panel` [geometry.panel_layout].

p13's panels are world choropleths on a graticule basemap with no key of their own, recorded `map-or-plan-view`; p11's caption says 'Identifying the critical nodes' but the drawing is an eighteen-column bar chart, so the family follows the ink [geometry.family].

Figure 9 on p15 reprints the Figure 6(a) artwork nearly pixel for pixel under its own caption; it is counted once as a printed exhibit per caption, and the reuse is declared in the note rather than silently dropped [caption.verbatim].

All six case-study plots share one template - 1970-2010 x axis, blue actual line, red '+' forecast markers, outside-right legend - except that Figure 10's y axis runs to 200 where the others stop at 160, so the scale is read per region and not assumed [geometry.legend].

Figure 2's three panels print as three separate small rasters in one row under one caption that splits them into '(a) (b)' and '(c)', so the caption is repeated verbatim on all three rows and the split is explained in each note [caption.verbatim].

Every heading is numbered (1.2.2, 2.2.1, 3.4, 3.5), so `section_path` quotes the printed heading and `section_numbered` is true throughout; p4 needs two routes because Figure 2 sits under 1.2.2 and Table 1 under 1.3 [place.section_path].

tables.note: The AQI band table, pasted in as a colour raster: header 'Air Quality Index Levels of Health Concern | Numerical Value | Meaning' over six bands, Good 0 to 50, Moderate 51 to 100, Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups 101 to 150, Unhealthy 151 to 200, Very Unhealthy 201 to 300, Hazardous 301 to 500. No rules at all: each band is a solid colour fill (green, yellow, orange, red, purple, maroon) and the white gaps between bands stand in for row rules, so `rule_style` is `no-rules` and `zebra` is false. The caption is the bare word 'Table 1' with no title.

The notation list: header 'Symbol | Meaning' over nine entries - f, g, d, r, p, F, q, S and l - with the symbols set in italic. Horizontal rules only, at the top, under the header and at the foot, plus two extra heavy rules that group the entries in threes; no vertical rules. One entry wraps to a second line inside its cell. The caption is the bare word 'Table 2' with no title. This table is live vector text, unlike the colour-grid Table 1 above it.

Input and output of the local network in one grid: a spanner header 'Input' over 'Name and Notation | Initial Value' and a spanner header 'Output' over 'Name and Notation | Type', then four body rows (population density, forest coverage rate, share of the secondary sector, sum of feedbacks to a global node). Two header rows, so `header_rows` is 2 and `merged_cells` is true; a vertical rule separates the Input half from the Output half, and horizontal rules run between every row. Two name cells wrap to three lines. The caption is the bare word 'Table 3' with no title.
